newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo believes can beat EU platinum worries.
newsitem.headline: Anglo believes can beat EU platinum worries.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd believes it could overcome any European Union worries about its strong stake in Lonrho Plc's platinum interests, group public affairs consultant Michael Spicer said.
"We are certainly aware of the European Community's interest in the subject and we remain confident that we can manage our way through the issue," he told Reuters on Thursday.

In April this year the European Commission blocked a merger between Impala Platinum Holdings and Lonrho's platinum mines because it was seen as anti-trust with the new company holding 28 percent of the world platinum market.

Seizing its chance then, the EU warned Anglo against taking control of Lonrho, saying it would pose the same problem because Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd already holds 35 percent of the world's platinum market.

Anglo on Tuesday swelled its stake in Lonrho to a direct 25.9 and indirect 2.2 percent stake, making it the largest shareholder by far and effectively giving it control of the British group and its assets, including Lonrho Platinum.
Lonrho is due to unbundle its business into separate mining, hotels and trading firms.
Anglo, while eager to develop its relationship with Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields through Lonrho's 30 percent stake, would not say whether it wanted Lonrho Platinum.
"I don't think I can comment on that," Spicer said.

Asked whether Anglo's purchase of former Lonrho chief executive Dieter Bock's remaining 18.3 percent stake on Tuesday was a blatant shrugging off of the EU's earlier warning, Spicer said: "No. We don't believe so."
Bock on Tuesday exercised his right to sell his shares at 180 pence per share.
Lonrho was trading in London on Thursday morning at around 150 pence.
